display.title: Tanya Shiur 32: The Soul Born to a King, and Tanya Chapter 15 Begins
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Tanya shiur: the double oath 'be a tzaddik, do not be a rasha', a Baal Shem Tov story about a holy soul, and chapter 15 on 'oved Elokim'.
display.summary_long: Shiur 32 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series, from the year the Rebbe called Shnas HaChinuch. After reviewing chapter 14, it explains the custom of throwing candies when a child first enters cheder and saying an angel threw them: Hashem gives every Jew the strength to understand Torah. The double oath 'be a tzaddik, do not be a rasha' means that even one who cannot become a tzaddik can always reach the level of a beinoni, and may be given a spark of a tzaddik's soul as a gift. A long story follows: the Baal Shem Tov blessed a childless couple, showed their son great love, and after the boy passed away at age three explained that a holy soul had once volunteered to be born to a king in order to save a Jewish community, and needed three more years with a Jewish mother. Chapter 15 then begins: 'oved Elokim' is a beinoni still in the middle of his work, while a tzaddik is called 'eved Hashem'. The names Havayeh and Elokim, Moshe's question about Hashem's name, the Baal Shem Tov and a crying child in a game of hide-and-seek, and the mashal of tanning leather explain the difference.
display.lesson: Hashem gives every Jew the strength to serve Him; one who works with all his strength is helped from Above.

date.note: Speaks of 'this year, Shnas HaChinuch' (5737); shiur 31a was given in Tishrei 5737, so probably late 1976.

study_text.note: Review and end of chapter 14; first part of chapter 15.

advisories.note: In a story, a young child dies suddenly at age three.
A king threatens to expel the Jews if he does not have a child.
A soul is judged in Heaven and sent back to the world; reincarnation is discussed.

characters: a priest who was secretly a Jew
